title: Charlie Christian and the tuberculosis story again
summary: He retells the fishing trip, Christian's hemorrhage and the rehearsal room.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Anyway, as far as Mr. Goodman is concerned, we spoke of Fletcher. You knew Charlie Christian pretty well?
And you said that you even caught tuberculosis.
You could never be certain where you caught it, but I suspect so, because he was pretty sick when he came with the band.

I remember in 1940 going fishing with Lionel and Irving Goodman and Lionel's wife, my wife and Charlie. I don't fish but I went along, it was fun to ride around the island on a boat, and he was pretty sick then. That was the first time I knew that he had
been. I know later on, that following winter, he had a hemorrhage on a plane.
Mel Powell was in that band and Mel got TB too.
They used to rehearse--didn't we put this on tape before, or were we just talking about it?
We talked about it; I don't think we taped it.

There was a room, maybe thirty by forty in which Benny used to rehearse and next to it was a studio with equipment. It couldn't have been more than twenty by twenty, it had a couch and a console and I used to have to stay in there and monitor the rehearsal; not as an engineer, just to be there. Charlie would come in and go on the couch, racked with TB and high with fever, and I'm sure he wanted to sleep, so he would come in. This was a year before I broke out. I suspect that might have had something to do with it. It affected my
life really after that. It took me out of the rat race, effectively.
